example.name: Zoe
example.look: medium brown skin, big curly brown hair, hearing aids

tagline: A toolbox, a broken bridge, and one kind question that changes everything.
lesson_or_purpose: Problems get solved by asking others what they need, and practical skills plus kindness can turn a grumpy stranger into a friend.
tone: Playful, cozy fairy-tale adventure with satisfying building sounds and a gentle, funny troll.
reading_level: Ages 3-8. Short sentences with sound words (tap, creak, clunk) and a light repeating refrain, easy to read aloud to younger children and simple enough for early readers.
illustration_guide: A cheerful storybook kingdom of rolling green hills, a small stone castle with round towers, and a wide blue river. Palette: soft sky blue, meadow green, warm honey gold, and berry red accents, with dusky purple for the shady space under the bridge. Recurring elements: the child in a simple crown and a practical tunic or dress with a tool belt, carrying a red wooden toolbox; a wooden bridge with a missing middle section; Bramble the troll, large, mossy-green, round-nosed, more shaggy than scary, with a patched blanket; a small blue bird that follows the child on every page; villagers with baskets and carts waiting on the far bank. Keep the troll friendly-looking even when grumpy: crossed arms and a pout, never sharp teeth.

page_outline.beat: Morning in the kingdom. {Princess/Prince} {name} is known for fixing things and is shown tightening a squeaky castle gate with a trusty red toolbox. Establish the refrain: tap, tap, twist, all better.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: A sunny castle courtyard with the child in a small crown kneeling by a wooden gate, using a little wrench from an open red toolbox, a blue bird perched on the gate.

page_outline.beat: A loud CREAK and CRACK echo from the river. The old bridge has a big broken gap in the middle, and villagers with carts of apples and bread cannot cross to market. {Princess/Prince} {name} grabs the toolbox and runs to help.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: A wide river with a wooden bridge missing its middle planks, villagers with carts and baskets looking worried on the far bank, the child running down the hill holding a red toolbox.

page_outline.beat: {name} measures the gap and starts hammering a new plank, but a rumbly voice booms from below: no more noise! Out climbs Bramble, a big, grumpy troll with crossed arms who lives under the bridge.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: The child holding a hammer at the edge of the broken bridge, startled, as a large mossy-green troll with crossed arms and a pout climbs up from the shady riverbank below.

page_outline.beat: Bramble grumbles that the bridge should stay broken. The villagers whisper that trolls are trouble. {Princess/Prince} {name} feels a little nervous but notices the troll looks more tired than mean.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: The troll standing tall and frowning beside the bridge, villagers peeking from behind a cart, and the child looking up at the troll with a curious, thoughtful face.

page_outline.beat: Instead of arguing, {name} sets down the hammer and asks a simple question: what do you need? Bramble is so surprised that the frown wobbles. Nobody has ever asked before.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: The child sitting on an upturned toolbox with hands open in a friendly way, the troll blinking in surprise, the blue bird tilting its head between them.

page_outline.beat: Bramble shows {Princess/Prince} {name} the home under the bridge. Rain drips through the old cracks onto a soggy bed, and stomping feet shake dust down all night. The troll has been cold, wet and sleepy for years.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: A cozy but damp nook under the bridge with a soggy patched blanket, puddles on the floor, drips falling from cracks in the planks above, the child and the troll looking up at the leaks together.

page_outline.beat: {name} has an idea and sketches a plan in the dirt with a stick: a bridge with tight, leak-proof planks, soft moss padding to hush the footsteps, and a snug little roof for the home below.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: The child crouching and drawing simple shapes in the dirt with a stick, the troll leaning in closely with a hopeful look, the toolbox open beside them.

page_outline.beat: The work begins. {Princess/Prince} {name} measures and hammers while Bramble lifts the heavy logs that no one else can carry. Tap, tap, twist. The villagers bring moss and rope to help too.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: The troll lifting a large log into place over the river while the child hammers a plank, villagers passing bundles of green moss and coils of rope along the bank.

page_outline.beat: A big storm rolls in before the last plank is done. {name} and Bramble work fast together in the rain, and the final plank clicks into place just in time. Not one drop leaks through.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: Dark rain clouds over the river, the child and the troll pressing the last plank into place side by side, raindrops bouncing off the smooth new bridge.

page_outline.beat: The sun comes out. Carts roll quietly across the soft, mossy bridge to market, and Bramble naps warm and dry below. {Princess/Prince} {name} learns that the best fix starts with asking what someone needs. Tap, tap, twist, all better.
page_outline.illustration_prompt: A sunny rainbow over the repaired bridge with villagers and carts crossing, the troll snoozing happily in a dry nook below, and the child waving from the middle of the bridge with the toolbox and the blue bird.

cover_scene: The child stands proudly in the middle of a sturdy wooden bridge over a sparkling blue river, wearing a small crown and a tool belt, holding a red toolbox. Beside the bridge, a big friendly mossy-green troll peeks up and smiles, and a little blue bird flies nearby. Rolling green hills and a small stone castle sit in the distance, with a wide calm pale-blue sky filling the top third of the picture.

sample_pages.text: Morning in the kingdom! {Princess/Prince} {name} fixes a squeaky gate. Tap, tap, twist. All better!
sample_pages.scene: A sunny castle courtyard where the child in a small crown kneels beside a wooden gate, turning a little wrench from an open red toolbox, while a blue bird watches from the top of the gate.

sample_pages.text: Under the bridge, drip, drip, drip! Rain fell on the troll's soggy bed. "So that is why you are grumpy," said {name}. "You need a dry home and a quiet night."
sample_pages.scene: A damp nook under the bridge with puddles and a soggy patched blanket, drips falling through cracks above, the child and the mossy troll looking up at the leaks side by side.

h1: Personalized Princess Book: Your Child Fixes the Broken Bridge
meta_title: Personalized Princess Book: The Broken Bridge | StoryBloom
meta_description: A personalized princess or prince book where your child grabs a toolbox, fixes a broken bridge and wins over a grumpy troll.
promise: Your child becomes a royal fixer who solves a real problem with tools, a clever plan and one kind question.
story_summary: Your child is the kingdom's handiest royal, always ready with a red toolbox. When the old bridge cracks and the villagers cannot reach market, your child rushes to repair it, only to be stopped by Bramble, a grumpy troll who lives underneath. Instead of arguing, your child asks the troll what he needs and discovers a soggy, sleepless home. Now there is a bigger job to do, and a storm is on the way.
why_parents: Between three and eight, children are learning that big feelings often have a reason behind them. This story shows a grumpy character who is not bad, just cold, wet and tired, and a hero who stops to find out why. It is a gentle way to practice curiosity over judgment.

It also gives your child a hero who builds things. Measuring, planning and hammering sit right alongside the crown, so the adventure celebrates being useful, capable and helpful, with teamwork turning a problem into a friendship.
for_grownups: Ask: Why do you think Bramble was grumpy at first? Have you ever felt grumpy because something was bothering you?
Practice the question from the story. Next time a sibling or friend is upset, try asking together: what do you need?
Build a pretend bridge from blocks or books and talk about what makes it strong, just like your child did in the story.

faqs.question: Can this book be a prince story instead of a princess story?
faqs.answer: Yes. The title and story use princess or prince to match your child, so the royal hero fits every reader.

faqs.question: Is the troll scary?
faqs.answer: Not at all. Bramble is grumpy at first with crossed arms and a pout, but is drawn soft and shaggy, and becomes a friend once your child asks what is wrong.

faqs.question: What will my child take away from the story?
faqs.answer: The story shows that asking someone what they need can solve a problem better than arguing. It also celebrates planning, building and working as a team.

feed_description: A personalized fairy tale adventure for ages 3 to 8 where your child is the royal hero with a red toolbox. When the kingdom's old bridge cracks and the villagers cannot reach market, your child rushes to repair it, but a grumpy troll named Bramble lives underneath and wants no more noise. Instead of arguing, your child asks a simple question: what do you need? Together they plan a leak-proof, mossy, quiet bridge and race to finish before a storm arrives. The story pairs building and problem solving with kindness and teamwork, and the gentle troll is friendly rather than scary. Works as a princess or prince story with your child's name and likeness throughout.
